propositions: The environment-variable registry scanner silently skips unrecognized os.environ attribute access forms (e.g., pop, setdefault) instead of failing, causing keys to drop from docs/env-vars.md without diagnostic signal.

A one-token refactor from os.environ.get() to os.environ.pop() reduces the generated registry count and removes documented variables while passing make lint locally, violating the invariant that new env-var reads cannot ship undocumented.

The recognizer at scripts/gen_env_registry.py:98 matches only get, subscript, and os.getenv forms plus KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS, leaving all other accessor methods to silently fall through the ast.walk loop with no error or diagnostic.

The fail-closed fix widens KEY_BEARING to include pop, setdefault, and __getitem__, and raises UnrecognisedEnvironAccess on any unclassified os.environ attribute access so novel forms abort the build rather than silently omit keys.

The local and CI verdicts are brought into agreement by adding python scripts/gen_env_registry.py --check to the make lint target, so staleness is caught immediately instead of only in the full suite.
